packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-16 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Exposure / process notes
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author. No edition, catalogue or earlier transcription was consulted.
- Visible in the images themselves are modern pencilled archival labels on the fragments: "Stams, STA, Fag. 35_1r", "35_2r", "35_3r", "35_4r" (face 1) and "35_1v" ... "35_4v" (face 2), and older pencil marks "IVa/M 25" (face 1) and "IVa/N 29" (face 2). The packet path also contains "stams4". These are shelfmark/provenance labels, not identifications of the text; I have not used them to interpret anything.
- Beyond the stated rules: I ran `ls` on the packet directory (to get the image filenames, excluding packet.json) and a one-line Python call to print the pixel sizes of the image files. I did not open any other file or directory.
- All 26 images loaded successfully.

Image map
- image-001: overview of face 1 (4 larger fragments + 2 tiny scraps on black cloth). image-002 to -013: native tiles of face 1, 4 across x 3 down, overlapping.
- image-014: overview of face 2 (same 4 fragments + 2 scraps, reverse sides). image-015 to -026: native tiles of face 2, same grid.
- Overlaps noted below; repeated lines in adjacent tiles are the same physical lines, not additional text.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Material looks like parchment, heavily stained, holed and cut; fragments are strips cut from one or more leaves (binding waste). Some pieces are repaired with transparent tape across a fold/crease.
- Script: small Gothic textualis/cursiva-influenced bookhand, dense abbreviation. Red ink used for rubric lines, paraph marks (C-shaped) before many lines, enlarged red initials (P, S, A, I, D, L, U, O), and red brace/bracket diagrams connecting lists of alternative words.
- Layout: at least two text columns per page with vertical ruling lines. Long prose passages alternate with vertical lists of single words or short phrases (many beginning with red paraphs), which are joined by red braces or star/fan-shaped red lines to a shared phrase - i.e. tables of interchangeable alternatives.
- Many red rubric lines read as instructions or section headings (e.g. "Hic pone conclusionem / et primo de affirmatiua", "multis modis", "de modis ad ...").
- Interlinear superscript additions appear in places (e.g. "sin" above a word in image-006).
- Tentative interpretation (not an identification): the content looks like a teaching text giving model phrases with lists of substitutable synonyms (petitions, salutation-type nouns of address such as Celsitudo / Magnificentia / Reuerentia, conclusions), with prose model passages. I do not infer author, work, date or provenance.
- Two tiny scraps (lower right of each overview) carry only a few letters.

Conventions: line numbers are counted from the top of the named tile, counting only lines of the fragment being transcribed. "]" = text cut at the edge of the fragment. "|" = a crease/taped fold or ruling the line crosses. Expansions in (), uncertain readings followed by (?), [illegible] where I could not read after close inspection. [red: ...] = text in red ink. "C-paraph" = red paragraph mark.
